transcript.text: Mr. Potter, please have a seat. I've been reviewing your latest diagnostic scans from your check-up. There's something... unusual. We're seeing magical residue in your neural pathways that doesn't match any standard post-combat diagnosis I've encountered. It appears to be lingering effects from your exposure to dark magic during the war, but the pattern is... irregular. I need to run deeper scans over the next several days, and I can't yet tell you whether this is something you'll recover from.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Okay, I understand. So, what you're saying is that the headaches and disorientation could be related to... some kind of lasting damage from the dark magic I encountered? I mean, I've had these moments for a while now, but I was just... hoping it was nothing serious.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Leans forward slightly, hands folded on the desk* Precisely. The symptoms you've described—headaches, disorientation, those moments of magical feedback—they align with what we're seeing. The concerning part is that this residue appears to be... active, in a sense. It's not just scar tissue from old curses; it's interacting with your natural magical core in ways we don't fully understand yet.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Active... right. I get it. So, what happens next? You mentioned deeper scans, but how long will that take? And... I mean, is there any chance this is... fixable? Or are we talking about a forever kind of thing?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Sighs softly, maintaining eye contact* We'll begin the scans tomorrow morning. They'll take several days—we need to monitor how the residue fluctuates with your magical activity. As for whether it's fixable... *pauses, choosing words carefully* I've seen curse damage that seemed permanent become manageable with time and proper treatment. But I've also seen cases where... well, the magic settles in ways that require long-term adaptation. I won't give you false hope, but I won't take all hope away either.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Got it. Thanks for... for not sugarcoating it. I appreciate that. So, what can I do in the meantime? Should I avoid using magic, or is it safe to keep on with my day-to-day? I don't want to make it worse, but I can't just... not use magic, you know?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Nods thoughtfully* A practical question. For now, continue with your daily activities but avoid any intensive magical exertion—no advanced spellwork, no prolonged dueling practice, nothing that would significantly drain your magical reserves. Keep a log of any symptoms that occur during or after magic use. The more data we have, the better we can understand what we're dealing with.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I can do that. I'll be... careful, I promise. I mean, I'm not exactly known for my light touch with magic, but I'll try to... tone it down a bit. And I'll definitely keep notes on anything that happens. It's just... I've been trying to get on with things, you know? Move past the war and all that. It's hard to accept that I might not be... fully recovered.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Voice softens slightly* Mr. Potter, surviving what you did is already a testament to your strength. This... this is just another part of that survival. Many who fought in the war carry scars that aren't visible to the eye. What matters now is understanding what we're facing so we can give you the best possible quality of life moving forward.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Quality of life... right. I guess I've been focusing on just... living, without really considering the quality part. Thanks... for... for not just giving up on me, or writing me off as some broken-down wizard. It's... appreciated. I'll do the scans, and the logging, and all that. What do I need to bring with me tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Offers a small, professional smile* Just yourself, Mr. Potter. We'll provide everything needed for the scans. Wear comfortable clothing—the diagnostic charms can be quite... thorough. And perhaps bring something to read; the sessions will last several hours each day. We'll start with the basic neural mapping at nine o'clock sharp.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Comfortable clothes... got it. And... I'll be there by nine. Thanks for... for handling this so... professionally. I know it's not every day you get someone with my... unique magical history walking in off the street. I'll be there, and I'll do what I can to help you help me. That's the best I can promise right now.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Stands, extending a hand* That's all we can ask for, Mr. Potter. Your cooperation will be invaluable. Until tomorrow morning, then. And remember—if anything changes or worsens before then, don't hesitate to come straight to the emergency ward.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood. I'll... I'll keep that in mind. It's... good to know that there's somewhere to go if... if things get worse. I'll be there at nine, and I'll do my best to stay out of trouble until then. Thanks... for your time. And... your hope. I think I needed that. See you tomorrow, then.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Nods, maintaining a calm, steady presence* Until tomorrow, Mr. Potter. Take care of yourself. The hope is yours to keep—I'm merely helping you carry it for a while.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I'll do that. Take care of myself, I mean. It's... been a while since I've had to do that. I've been so... focused on everyone else, and... it's time I... I took care of me, too. Thanks for... for the reminder. I'll... see you tomorrow. Goodnight, Doctor.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Gives a slight, respectful nod* Goodnight, Mr. Potter. Rest well—it will help with the scans. We'll see this through together.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Together... right. I'll... try to rest. Thanks. I... I'm not sure how to feel about all this, but... I'll just have to figure it out. I always... seem to do that, don't I? Take care, Doctor. I'll be there at nine.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Offers a final, professional nod* That you do, Mr. Potter. That you do. Nine o'clock. We'll begin then. Safe travels home.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
